one_line: Rival South Indian kings standing at the turning point between Pallava rule and Chola expansion in Tondaimandalam, c. 897 CE.

appearance.age_look: Aditya I: mid-30s, athletic and broad-shouldered; Aparajita: late-30s to early-40s, slightly taller, lean but strong.
appearance.face: Aditya I has an oval face, medium-brown Dravidian complexion, sharp nose, strong jaw, a small tilaka on the forehead, and a focused, determined expression; Aparajita has a slightly longer face, similar complexion, prominent nose, neatly trimmed moustache, and a calm but alert, contemplative gaze.
appearance.hair: Aditya I’s thick black hair is tied in a high warrior topknot (kudumi) with a narrow gold band at the base, sides neatly drawn back; Aparajita’s black hair is gathered into a lower, slightly longer topknot wrapped with a thin white cloth strip and a small central gold disc at the front hairline.
appearance.costume: Aditya I wears a deep-red silk upper cloth (angavastram) diagonally over the left shoulder and across the chest, covering a short-sleeved, close-fitting off‑white cotton tunic, paired with a golden‑yellow cotton veshti (dhoti) wrapped to mid‑calf and pleated in front, bordered with a simple maroon stripe; his waist is cinched with a plain leather belt, feet in brown leather sandals, arms adorned with modest gold armlets and bangles, and a small Chola tiger emblem worked subtly on the belt buckle; Aparajita wears a pale‑cream, finely woven cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders like a shawl, covering a light‑grey, short‑sleeved tunic, and a soft, pale‑blue veshti with a dark‑blue border, wrapped slightly higher for ease of movement, secured at the waist with a cloth girdle and a simple rectangular bronze clasp, his feet in dark leather sandals, jewellery limited to a single strand gold necklace and understated armlets, reflecting older Pallava restraint; both outfits are modest, fully covering torso and legs, with no bare chest and no exposed thighs.
appearance.signature: Aditya I carries a long, slightly curved iron sword with a plain bronze hilt and simple wooden scabbard hanging from his belt, while Aparajita holds a round wooden shield faced with dark hide and a central bronze boss, used more as a symbol of his defensive stance than aggression.

ref_desc: Athletic Aditya I with medium-brown oval face, black high topknot, deep-red angavastram over off-white tunic, golden-yellow veshti and sword at belt stands beside lean Aparajita with lower topknot, cream shawl, grey tunic, pale-blue veshti and round dark shield, in reds, yellows, creams, blues and browns.
sheet_prompt: Draw an anime-style full-body model sheet of two South Indian kings from c. 897 CE standing side by side: Aditya I Chola and Aparajita Pallava. Aditya I is in his mid-30s, athletic and broad-shouldered, with a medium-brown Dravidian complexion, oval face, sharp nose, strong jaw, small tilaka on his forehead and a focused, determined expression; his thick black hair is pulled into a high warrior topknot with a narrow gold band at its base. He wears a deep-red silk angavastram draped diagonally from his left shoulder across his chest over a close-fitting, short-sleeved off‑white cotton tunic, modestly covering his torso, and a golden‑yellow cotton veshti (dhoti) wrapped to mid‑calf with a simple maroon border, fully covering his legs. A plain leather belt with a small Chola tiger motif on the buckle holds a long, slightly curved iron sword in a wooden scabbard at his left hip; he has simple gold armlets and bangles and brown leather sandals. Beside him, Aparajita Pallava is late-30s to early-40s, slightly taller and lean but strong, with a similar medium-brown complexion, longer face, prominent nose, neatly trimmed moustache and a calm but alert gaze; his black hair is gathered into a lower, slightly longer topknot wrapped with a thin white cloth and a small circular gold disc at the front hairline. He wears a pale‑cream, fine cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders like a shawl, covering a light‑grey short-sleeved tunic, and a pale‑blue veshti with a dark‑blue border, wrapped slightly higher for ease of movement and secured with a cloth girdle and simple bronze clasp, all modest and fully covering his torso and legs; his jewellery is restrained—a single strand gold necklace and understated armlets. On his left arm he carries a round wooden shield faced with dark hide and a central bronze boss, held down by his side as a symbol of defense, and he wears dark leather sandals. Keep the styling shonen-anime with energetic linework but historically grounded draped garments, no anachronisms, and a clear colour palette of deep red, golden yellow, pale cream, pale blue, greys and dark browns, showing them front and three-quarter views so their fixed hairstyles, costumes and signature sword and shield can be redrawn consistently.
